about.title: San Dimas Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: San Dimas sees its share of traffic collisions where the SR-57 and SR-210 freeways meet local roads like Arrow Highway, and the numbers back that up: 139 injury collisions and 204 injured people in the most recent recorded year, plus 3 traffic deaths. Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. tend to bring more reported crashes, likely tied to commuter traffic funneling toward the freeway interchanges. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, what happens in the days right after matters. Insurance adjusters move fast, and evidence like skid marks, vehicle damage, and witness memory fade quickly. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect injured people in San Dimas with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the crash, deal with insurers, and help protect your right to recover. There's no cost to you unless your attorney recovers money on your behalf.

whyChoose.title: Why San Dimas Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: The clock is running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like Los Angeles County or Caltrans on SR-57/SR-210 — may be involved. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before it's too late.

items.title: Fault isn't all-or-nothing
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash — your recovery is simply reduced by your share of fault. An independent attorney can help make sure the insurance company doesn't unfairly inflate your percentage of blame.

items.title: No fee unless you recover
items.desc: Attorneys in the LawProactive network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to have your case reviewed. You also don't have to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement before speaking with someone who represents your interests.

items.question: Do I have to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: No, you're not required to give a recorded statement to the other side's insurer, and it's often better not to before speaking with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to reduce or deny your claim. An independent attorney can talk to the insurer on your behalf instead.

items.question: What if my crash happened at a freeway interchange like SR-57 and SR-210?
items.answer: Crashes near freeway interchanges can involve state highway design or maintenance, which sometimes brings a government agency like Caltrans into the picture. Claims against government entities in California can have a much shorter filing deadline, sometimes just six months, so it's worth having an attorney look at the details of where and how the crash happened as soon as possible.

items.question: Is there a cap on how much I can recover for pain and suffering in California?
items.answer: No, California does not cap non-economic damages such as pain and suffering in most personal injury cases stemming from a car accident. Your recovery instead depends on the facts of your case, including the severity of your injuries and how fault is divided. An attorney can help evaluate what a fair claim might look like based on your specific situation.
